p:cNvPr.descr: An image depicting the role of biotin in the pyruvate carboxylase reaction. This begins on the left with a pink HCO3-, which has an arrow to the right pointing to pyruvate carboxylase. This arrow has a curved arrow pointing from ATP to ADP. This arrow also has another arrow jetting to Pi. Pyruvate carboxylase begins with a pentagon on the left. The top left point double bonds up and left to O. The top right point is NH. The bottom left point is N, which bonds down and left to (all pink) C, which double bonds down to O and bonds left to O-. Another pentagon shares the bottom right side. The bottom right point of this pentagon is S. The top right point bonds right, then down, the right. At this point, it bonds down and left, then down and right, where it double bonds to O. It then bonds down and left to NH, which bonds down to Lys. Continuing on at the point it bonded down, it bonds right, then up and left, then right, then to the top left point of a pentagon. The bottom left point is S. This pentagon shares its top right side with another pentagon. The top left of this pentagon is NH. The top right double bonds up and right to O, and the bottom right point is N, which bonds down and right to (all in pink) C, which bonds right to O- and double bonds down to O. A curved dashed arrow points from the first NH to the NH in this pentagon. To the right is an arrow pointing right to pyruvate. In blue, C double bonds up and left to O, bonds down and left to O-, which bonds right to C. C bonds up to O-. A red arrow bonds from the negative sign to this bond line. C also double bonds right to CH2. Form this double bond is a red arrow pointing to CO2. To the right is a right arrow pointing to oxaloacetate, which begins with C, which double bonds up and left to O, bonds down and left to O-, and right to C, which double bonds up to O, and bonds right to CH2 (all in blue). CH2 also bonds right to (all in pink) C, which double bonds up and right to O and bonds down and right to O-.
